articles.title: The Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. Announces New Hours for Spring
articles.deck: Residents of Tannery Flats filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for book exchange box along Rail Road, with work expected to start in September. The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Vincent Orchard, who has lived in Tannery Flats for 15 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Tannery Flats Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Public works estimates the work will take about 15 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Winter Coat Drive
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood filled the hall on Friday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Dominic Tiernan, who has lived in Bellwood for 13 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The group has raised $850 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Public works estimates the work will take about 13 weeks once it begins. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
The plan calls for winter coat drive along Beacon Terrace, with work expected to start in June.

articles.title: Council Tables Neighborhood Watch Sign Program Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 18 residents spoke at Thursday’s session.
body: Residents of Canal Park said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Public works estimates the work will take about 18 weeks once it starts in November.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Councilmember Patrice Chandler asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: The Mill Hill Lions Club Hosts Pocket Park on Friday
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
The event will be held at the Millrace library, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Friday. Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Elementary Board Approves Neighborhood Watch Sign Program
articles.deck: The program begins in March and is open to all students in grade 3 and up.
body: Principal Rosalind Jablonski said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for March.
Students will meet on Wednesday afternoons in the Hickory Ridge rec center, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. The board will review the results at the end of the summer term.

articles.title: Letters: Prospect Terrace Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the May meeting. Please keep the community oven in the budget. Many of us on Prospect Terrace use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Gordon Ingersoll, Eastgate

articles.title: Yolanda Marchetti, 76, Longtime Crossing Guard
articles.deck: Friends remember Yolanda Marchetti for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge.
